title: Indirect Field-Oriented Control of an Induction Machine Fed by an Advanced Multilevel Converter for Electric Vehicle Applications: A Comparative Analysis with a Cascaded Structure
content: This paper presents a rigorous comparison of two three-phase, five-level inverters intended to supply a squirrel-cage induction machine. Such reduced-component multilevel structures are of particular interest for electric-vehicle traction drives, where a lower switch and gate-driver count directly benefits converter cost, volume, and reliability. The first structure, adopted as the reference, is a cascaded H-bridge inverter comprising two cells per phase, i.e., twenty-four controlled switches and six isolated DC sources. The second combines a classical H-bridge with an auxiliary level-selection cell and requires only fifteen controlled switches together with twelve diodes for the three legs as a whole. Both converters are coupled to the same machine and subjected to an indirect field-oriented control scheme aligned with the rotor flux, to a level-shifted carrier PWM, to identical regulators, and to identical test scenarios. Topology is thus the sole variable under study. The structural analysis shows that the second configuration reduces the number of controlled switches and gate-drive circuits by 37.5%. On the other hand, it increases the total number of power components, since the four additional diodes per phase outnumber the three switches removed. It likewise raises the total blocking voltage by 12.5% and doubles the individual blocking voltage of four switches per phase. The reduction in the number of isolated DC sources, made possible by sharing a common bus among the three cells, is demonstrated analytically but is not verified by simulation. Electrical and dynamic performance are investigated under MATLAB/Simulink for three speed references and two torque steps, using indicators related to harmonic distortion, speed tracking, and flux-orientation quality. The simulated waveforms of the electrical and mechanical quantities confirm the proper operation and effectiveness of both converters.
